newsitem.title: HONG KONG: BOC sees Hong Kong as center of Asian debt market.
newsitem.headline: BOC sees Hong Kong as center of Asian debt market.

text.p: Hong Kong after 1997 has the unique potential to become the Asian regional debt market, said Bank of China Hong Kong branch general manager Yang Zilin at a seminar in Hong Kong on Thursday.
"Hong Kong can offer a full range of services to China-based issuers of debt," said Yang.

"Hong Kong has made many a big effort to facilitate the development of its debt market," he said. "The territory has a high degree of openness which is very attractive to overseas-based issuers of debt."

Measures that the Hong Kong government has taken in the current financial year to stimulate the development of the debt market include a 50 percent reduction in the tax on interest income and commission earned on the sale of bonds and other debt instruments, Yang said.
The central money markets unit of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, which should be in operation soon, will facilitate the settlement of bonds sales to the general public, he noted.
